cv-6db081fa.stem: A patient gets dizzy with blurred vision after using the left arm for a long time; the blood pressure in the left arm is clearly lower than in the right. Angiography shows a stenosis at the origin of the left subclavian artery. What is the mechanism of the symptoms?
options: Reversed flow in the left internal carotid artery
Occlusion of the internal thoracic artery
Occlusion of the right vertebral artery
Reversed flow in the left vertebral artery (subclavian steal syndrome)
cv-6db081fa.explanation: When the stenosis lies before the origin of the vertebral artery, exercise of the arm 'steals' blood from the brainstem through the left vertebral artery towards the arm; symptoms of vertebrobasilar insufficiency appear.

cv-cf804f79.stem: The artery most often used as a graft in coronary bypass surgery, with the best long-term patency, is a branch of which artery?
cv-cf804f79.explanation: The internal thoracic (internal mammary) artery arises from the first part of the subclavian artery and descends close to the sternal border. Anastomosing the left internal thoracic artery to the LAD (LIMA–LAD) gives the best long-term results.

cv-94f2afe5.stem: Which artery is NOT a branch of the thyrocervical trunk?
cv-94f2afe5.explanation: The thyrocervical trunk arises from the subclavian artery and gives the inferior thyroid artery (whose branch is the ascending cervical artery), the suprascapular artery and the transverse cervical artery. The superior thyroid artery is the first branch of the ECA.

cv-1a1c0e40.stem: Which of the following is a branch of the third part of the axillary artery?
cv-1a1c0e40.explanation: First part (above pectoralis minor): superior thoracic artery. Second part (behind it): thoraco-acromial and lateral thoracic arteries. Third part (below it): subscapular artery and the anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries. The internal thoracic artery arises from the subclavian artery.

cv-04d706e5.stem: If the axillary artery is ligated between the thyrocervical trunk and the subscapular artery, which collateral network keeps the arm supplied?
options: Scapular anastomosis (suprascapular, dorsal scapular and circumflex scapular arteries)
cv-04d706e5.explanation: Around the scapula, branches of the subclavian artery (suprascapular and dorsal scapular arteries) anastomose with the subscapular branch of the axillary artery (circumflex scapular artery). So if the ligature lies between these branches, the arm remains supplied.

cv-90c880be.stem: Which artery runs with the radial nerve in the radial groove?
cv-90c880be.explanation: The profunda brachii is the largest branch in the arm and runs with the radial nerve in the groove on the back of the humerus; it supplies the posterior compartment of the arm and joins the anastomosis around the elbow.

cv-2354b9a9.stem: At the wrist, the radial pulse is felt just lateral to which tendon?
cv-2354b9a9.explanation: At the wrist the radial artery runs superficially in front of the distal end of the radius, lateral to the FCR tendon, and is felt by pressing it against the bone. It then crosses the floor of the snuffbox to the back of the hand.

cv-47f821c9.stem: The Allen test is performed before radial artery cannulation in intensive care. What is the purpose of the test?
options: To check whether the hand is adequately supplied through the ulnar artery and the palmar arches
To test the function of the median nerve
To detect a stenosis of the brachial artery
To measure the wall thickness of the radial artery
cv-47f821c9.explanation: The radial and ulnar arteries are compressed together and the hand blanches; then the ulnar artery is released. Rapid return of colour shows that the ulnar artery and superficial palmar arch are adequate and that the hand can be supplied even if the radial artery occludes.

cv-f33acf1b.stem: Which artery mainly forms the superficial palmar arch?
cv-f33acf1b.explanation: The superficial palmar arch is mainly the continuation of the ulnar artery, completed by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery; the deep palmar arch is formed mainly by the radial artery and lies more proximally.

cv-949621d9.stem: The common interosseous artery is a branch of which artery?
cv-949621d9.explanation: Just below the cubital fossa the ulnar artery gives off the common interosseous artery, which divides into the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries running in front of and behind the interosseous membrane.

cv-182b9c31.stem: Over which artery is the stethoscope placed when blood pressure is measured?
cv-182b9c31.explanation: The cuff is wrapped around the arm; the stethoscope is placed in the cubital fossa over the brachial artery, just medial to the biceps tendon. The Korotkoff sounds are heard here.

cv-80e9ff2a.stem: What are the three branches of the coeliac trunk?
options: Inferior phrenic artery, splenic artery, common hepatic artery
Left gastric artery, splenic artery, common hepatic artery
Right gastric artery, splenic artery, proper hepatic artery
Left gastric artery, gastroduodenal artery, renal artery
Gastroduodenal artery, splenic artery, superior mesenteric artery
cv-80e9ff2a.explanation: The coeliac trunk arises from the front of the aorta at T12 and supplies the foregut derivatives (abdominal oesophagus, stomach, upper duodenum, liver, gallbladder, part of the pancreas and the spleen).

cv-929f7309.stem: A patient with a history of peptic ulcer presents with massive haematemesis. Endoscopy shows a bleeding ulcer on the posterior wall of the first part of the duodenum. Which artery is most likely bleeding?
cv-929f7309.explanation: The gastroduodenal artery arises from the common hepatic artery and descends just behind the first part of the duodenum. Posterior wall ulcers erode this artery and cause serious bleeding; anterior wall ulcers tend to perforate instead.

cv-ed78d041.stem: Which statement about the splenic artery is false?
options: It is the largest branch of the coeliac trunk.
It runs a tortuous course along the upper border of the pancreas.
It supplies the fundus of the stomach through the short gastric arteries.
It reaches the spleen in the splenorenal ligament.
It gives off the right gastro-omental (gastroepiploic) artery.
cv-ed78d041.explanation: The splenic artery gives the left gastro-omental artery and the short gastric arteries. The right gastro-omental artery is a branch of the gastroduodenal artery; the two gastro-omental arteries anastomose along the greater curvature of the stomach.

cv-9dcf655b.stem: What area does the superior mesenteric artery supply?
options: The bowel from the middle of the descending part of the duodenum to about the left third of the transverse colon
From the oesophagus to the middle of the duodenum
From the left third of the transverse colon to the upper rectum
cv-9dcf655b.explanation: The SMA (L1) supplies the midgut derivatives: the duodenum beyond the major papilla, jejunum, ileum, caecum, appendix, ascending colon and the proximal 2/3 of the transverse colon. Its branches: inferior pancreaticoduodenal, jejunal and ileal arteries, ileocolic, right colic and middle colic arteries.
